openings.claim: Fixed captive plywood end stops replace operator-selected insertion depth with rod-end contact in loose crossed channels. Supplied cord/elastic keeps clearance keepers and hardware captive without closing pressure. This tests positioning alone; loaded pointer stability is unestablished.
openings.discriminator: Compare identical channels with active stops versus captive stops disengaged and ruler-set depth. If depth variation materially contributes, active stops should reduce unloaded exchange displacement. If clearance, seating angle or rod-size change dominates, repeatable contact may leave or increase error. The tighter-fit observation prevents assuming tighter channels improve return.
openings.probe: Use only supplied plywood, hardware, tethers and tools; no clamp preload or rod modification. Only hand-operated assembly/adjustment; no drilling, adhesive or permanent rod marks. Keep the complete assembly within a 90 mm cube and every component captive during exchange; check captivity/envelope first. Fabricate one fixture with active/disengaged captive stop positions within 100 minutes. Within 20 testing minutes, perform twelve exchanges per configuration: five per original rod, then two with the 18 mm replacement. Log exchange times and target displacement. Apply four ten-second 10 N lateral trials each after exchanges 2, 6, 10 and 12; compare return/loaded displacement with target card, ruler and scale.
openings.uncertainty: Offcuts, eight bolts and tethers sufficing for channels, stops and captive clearance keepers within fabrication time is unverified. Observable, comparable stop contact without rod alteration is assumed. Fabrication or timing failure leaves comparison unresolved. Defeats: no return improvement, missed 2 mm target, movement during load, any exchange taking forty seconds or more, or failure with the 18 mm rod. Passive channel clearance may prevent the valued outcome.

lineage.reason: Positioning relation, rival, predictions, full probe, defeat conditions, resource caveats and declared uncertainty preserved.

decision: Retain the uncertain stop-only comparison. No deployment or reliable performance is established; success requires return within 2 mm after five exchanges each and remaining there throughout load.
